game.name: Exit the Gungeon

commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Exit the Gungeon is the spin-off follow-up to Enter the Gungeon, originally built with mobile in mind, so it is far more minimalistic. It is a side-on 2D bullet hell with cramped space, fast runs and randomly swapping guns. He finds the gameplay boring and dislikes the RNG design, and he beat it on his first run. Its gorgeous remodeled Gungeon art and characters save it from a low placement, and he puts it above Enter the Gungeon on the board.
praise: Art style is straight Gungeon and looks awesome
Characters were remodeled rather than reusing sprites
Nostalgic to see the Gungeon cast alive again
Runs are much faster than the original
criticism: Gameplay is not really fun and feels kind of boring
Very minimalistic compared to Enter the Gungeon, disappointing as a follow-up
Much less space to dodge bullets in the side-on view, which feels awkward
Random gun swapping with no gun collection; snowballing when you get strong guns
Too easy: he beat it on his first run
unique_points: Guns switch randomly after a few seconds instead of being collected
Side-on 2D perspective rather than top-down for a bullet hell
Strong guns make better guns more likely, creating a snowball effect
commentary.quote: I can't put this super low because look at the art style
design_criteria: Charm/visuals: art style and remodeled characters carry the placement
Gameplay feel: found it unfun and boring
Randomness: random gun swapping feels weird and snowballs
Space/level design: cramped side-on arena limits dodging
Difficulty: beat it on the first run

community.one_liner: A 2D vertical bullet-hell platformer spin-off of Enter the Gungeon where the Gungeoneers ride a collapsing elevator upward, with a blessed gun that keeps morphing into random weapons.
community.consensus_summary: Exit the Gungeon is received as a competent but clearly lesser spin-off: critics land in mixed-to-decent territory (Metacritic 68 Switch / 67 PC, about 45% of OpenCritic critics recommending) and Steam players are Mostly Positive at about 74% across roughly 3,800 reviews. Most praise the chaotic arcade energy, art, humor and bosses, while criticising the forced random gun-swapping, cramped arenas and reduced depth versus Enter the Gungeon. It began life as an Apple Arcade mobile title (Sept 2019) before reaching Switch/PC (Mar 2020), and many negative reviews are really 'this is not Enter the Gungeon' complaints. A late content update (Hello to Arms, adding an Arsenal Mode with normal weapon pickups) softened the biggest complaint, but a Meowitzer boss softlock bug is still reported in recent Steam reviews. It is a cheap, often-discounted short-session game rather than a long-term roguelite.
best_things: Frantic, nonstop arcade bullet-hell action with very little downtime and short runs that suit quick sessions
Same Gungeon charm: humor, weapon designs, pixel art and animation, soundtrack and sound design
Boss fights that remix the original's bosses into fusion bosses with new attack patterns
Per-character elevator routes and a new vertical structure give it a distinct feel from the first game
Unlockable hats, new costumes and small extras (Winchester and Loblina minigames, robot hearts now useful, Cultist playable without co-op) that completionists enjoy
Cheap price and frequent sales make it decent value as a pickup-and-play game
worst_things: Constantly changing blessed gun means you rarely build toward anything; combo-based weapon quality still delivers junk guns at bad moments
Meowitzer boss bug (boss turns invisible, softlocks or kills the run) is reported by many reviewers and persists years later
Elevator arenas are small, flat and cramped, leaving little room for dodging or platforming; enemies spawn constantly
Much less content and depth than Enter the Gungeon: no synergies, little new enemy/gun/music content, runs feel repetitive quickly
Jump-immunity and dodge-roll spam can trivialise bullets and some bosses instead of rewarding skillful movement
Stiff/odd controls and sometimes disorienting camera, cluttered visuals that hide hazards, and moving shooting platforms in later stages
Feels like a simplified, mobile-origin spin-off rather than a true sequel; the most upvoted negative reviews are fans saying it is not Enter the Gungeon and forces blessed-style runs on them
improvements: Fix the Meowitzer softlock and other audio/visual bugs
Offer more freedom over weapons by default (normal pickups/synergies) instead of relying on blessed guns; Arsenal Mode only partially addresses this
Larger, more varied arenas with real platforming space and less spawn spam
More new content (guns, enemies, characters, music) rather than recycled assets from Enter the Gungeon
Tuning of blanks, hazards and weapon rolls so randomness feels less unfair
unique_things: Vertical elevator-climb structure instead of exploring a branching dungeon
Weapon auto-morphs every ~30 seconds, with quality tied to a hitless kill combo (0-20)
Jumping grants airborne invulnerability, making jump a core defensive tool alongside rolling
Bosses are fusions of Enter the Gungeon bosses
Hub (Underbreach) with NPCs and small minigames like Angry-Birds-style and pachinko-style games
Began as an Apple Arcade exclusive and was designed as an arcade-style bite-sized spin-off
tedious_or_disliked: Forced elevator waves in early levels feel tedious and repetitive
Random weapon swaps at bad moments, and combo reset on any hit, feel punishing rather than fun
100%-ing the game becomes grindy; reviewers describe it as dragging after the main content is done
Repeated boss and enemy reuse and small gun pool make runs feel samey after a few characters
Getting Meowitzer repeatedly and needing to restart runs because of the bug
Levels feel flat and compact, with little platforming space, making later runs a grind of dodging spawn waves
divisive_points: Blessed/random weapon system: some find it chaotic fun, many find it the game's biggest flaw
Comparison to Enter the Gungeon: defenders say it should be judged as a different arcade game, detractors call it a creative failure and letdown for fans
Difficulty: some say it is very hard (bosses, tiny arenas), others find it easy once jump-dodging is discovered
Value: cheap sale price seen as fair for what it is, but others feel even that is too much
community.reception_notes: Launched Sept 2019 on Apple Arcade, then Mac/Windows/Switch in March 2020, PS4/Xbox One in Nov 2020, and separate iOS/Android releases in Aug 2025 per Wikipedia. Critics were mixed (71% of Metacritic Switch reviews rated Mixed, none Negative); the random-gun mechanic and loss of depth were the main sticking points. Steam is Mostly Positive (about 74%), with negative reviews heavily focused on the Meowitzer softlock, forced blessed-style runs and disappointment versus Enter the Gungeon. Final update Hello to Arms added Arsenal Mode for normal weapon pickups per a Steam reviewer. Steam has roughly 200k-500k owners (SteamSpy) and an estimated $1.17M gross / $345k net revenue (steam-revenue-calculator.com, Boxleiter-method estimate, not audited). Price $9.99, often on deep sale. Windows only on Steam, no Mac/Linux listing there. Steam recent reviews continue through 2026, indicating an ongoing trickle of players and a still-present boss bug. Caveat: live web search budget was exhausted, so Reddit was not reachable and community themes come mainly from Steam reviews, Metacritic, Wikipedia and the Steam discussions page.
